title: Security and Compliance: Integrated Playbook — RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency & Retention, Secure SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows, Risk & Exceptions
author: Ariana Patel
content:
Overview:

This integrated playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's security- and compliance-related procedures across RBAC & authentication, audit logging, data residency & retention, secure SDLC, incident response security, compliance evidence workflows, and risk/exception handling. It is intended for control owners, engineering leads, security engineers, and compliance reviewers.

Purpose and scope:
- Provide a single reference for operational controls and evidence collection required for internal and external audits (SOC2, ISO27001, GDPR assessments).
- Define owners, SLOs, retention windows, and the end-to-end steps for exception requests and remediation.
- Apply to Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployment modes (customer-specific requirements may add constraints).

1) RBAC & Authentication

Principles:
- Least privilege by default; grant access only for specific tasks and revoke promptly when no longer needed.
- Role-based assignment combined with group membership via SSO.
- All human access authenticated via company SSO (Okta) + MFA; machine identities use short-lived cert/token flows.

Roles and ownership (examples):
- security-admin: full control for security team (owner: security@redwood.com)
- platform-admin: infra and deployment control (owner: eng-infra)
- svc-account-readonly: read-only telemetry access for monitoring tools (owner: eng-sre)

Authentication methods:
- Primary: SAML SSO (Okta) with enforced MFA (TOTP or WebAuthn).
- Service-to-service: Vault-issued short-lived mTLS certificates or OAuth2 client credentials with rotating secrets managed by Vault.
- API keys: issued only for external integrations, stored in KMS/HSM, rotated every 90 days by default.

RBAC lifecycle and controls:
1. Access request using the internal access portal (link: /tools/access-requests).
2. Justification and TTL required for elevated access; TTL default = 24h for emergency access.
3. Access reviews: quarterly automated reviews for admin roles; owners must attest.
4. Deprovisioning: integrate with HR offboarding; access removed within 4 hours of termination event.

Enforcement / technical controls:
- IAM policy snippets enforced in IAM and application-layer ACLs.
- Audited group membership exported to central compliance index daily.

2) Audit Logging

Goals:
- Provide immutable, searchable logs for authentication, authorization decisions, admin actions, configuration changes, and data access to satisfy forensic and compliance requirements.

What to log (minimum):
- Authentication events (login, SSO, MFA challenges)
- Authorization decisions (allow/deny) for privileged routes and admin consoles
- Configuration changes to runtime, routing policies, and model pinning
- Data export/downloads and access to customer-managed private deployments
- Admin actions (role grants, exception approvals, policy changes)
- Incident response actions (investigation notes, containment steps)

Log retention and protection:
| Log category | Minimum retention | Storage location | Access control |
|--------------|-------------------|------------------|----------------|
| Auth & AuthZ | 2 years           | Central logging (ELK/Hot-Warm) | security + audits only (RBAC) |
| API & admin | 1 year            | Central logging | eng-sre + security (read) |
| Forensics    | 3 years            | Immutable S3 (WORM) | security (restricted) |

Integrity controls:
- All logs signed and shipped via the logging agent to the central pipeline; original agent logs retained for 30 days locally.
- Immutable snapshots (WORM) created monthly for forensics-critical logs.
- Access to log retention configuration is restricted to security-admin and platform-admin roles.

Monitoring & alerting:
- Real-time alerts for: repeated failed auth attempts (> 10 within 10 minutes), privilege escalation events, and export requests for customer data.
- SLO: mean time to acknowledge high-priority auth/privilege alerts <= 15 minutes.

3) Data Residency & Retention

Policy summary:
- Customer data is stored in the region specified in the customer contract/console; default region: us-west-2 for US customers, eu-central-1 for EU customers.
- Cross-region replication requires explicit customer consent or contractual clause.

Data classification and retention windows (examples):
- PII (customer account data): retain 7 years unless contract specifies otherwise.
- Usage telemetry (non-PII aggregated): retain 1 year for product analytics, 90 days for raw detailed telemetry unless needed for incident investigation.
- Audit logs: follow the Audit Logging table above.

Encryption and key management:
- Data at rest encrypted using AES-256; keys managed in AWS KMS or customer-managed BYOK/HSM for Private deployments.
- In transit: TLS 1.2+ with strong ciphers; service-to-service mutual TLS for sensitive internal APIs.

Retention & deletion workflows:
1. Data subject / deletion requests: route to privacy-triage@redwood.com; standard DSAR SLA = 30 days.
2. Automated retention sweeper runs weekly to delete objects past retention; deletions logged and retained for audit (deletion receipts).
3. Backup retention aligned with primary retention; backups older than retention are purged by lifecycle rules.

4) Secure SDLC (Secure Software Development Lifecycle)

Requirements for code and releases:
- All production code must pass: automated unit tests, static application security testing (SAST), dependency vulnerability scanning (OSS scanning), and an approved change review.
- Pull request policy: at least one security reviewer on PRs touching security-sensitive subsystems (auth, secrets, runtime).
- Secrets: secrets must never be checked into source control; use Vault or KMS and automated scanners to detect accidental commits.

Build and deployment controls:
- CI pipeline signs artifacts; signed artifacts are required for production deployment.
- Image hardening: base images scanned and rebuilt monthly; package updates applied per severity (critical within 24 hours).
- Feature flags: sensitive features roll out via canary with telemetry and quality gates.

Supply chain and third-party management:
- Approved dependencies registry maintained by eng-developer-experience; unapproved dependencies blocked in CI.
- Third-party vendor security review required for any service with access to customer data.

Security testing cadence:
- Quarterly external pentests on critical infra.
- Continuous fuzzing and automated regression tests in the eval-harness for model-serving components.

5) Incident Response — Security Procedures

Activation and triage:
1. Detection: alerts from monitoring, customer reports, or internal discovery.
2. Triage: first responder (on-call security engineer) creates an incident record in the incident tracker and assigns priority (P1/P2/P3).
3. Containment: apply short-term mitigations (isolate nodes, revoke keys, throttle routes).

Roles & responsibilities:
- Incident Commander (IC): coordinates cross-functional response (owner: on-call security lead)
- SRE Lead: executes containment and remediation in infra
- Product/Model Owner: assesses customer-impacting regressions
- Communications Lead: external and internal comms (status page updates, legal notification if required)

Investigation and evidence preservation:
- Preserve logs and system images to immutable storage (forensics S3) before any destructive remediation.
- Document chain of custody for exported artifacts.
- Collect timeline of events, affected services, and initial IOC list.

Post-incident:
- Blameless postmortem within 72 hours (draft) and a prioritized action plan within 10 business days.
- Action items tracked in a dedicated tickets board with owners and SLA for closure.

Notification thresholds (examples):
- Customer-impacting data exposure: notify affected customers within contractual SLA and escalate to legal.
- Regulatory thresholds (e.g., GDPR breach): follow legal threshold timelines for regulator notification.

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows

Evidence lifecycle:
1. Control owner identifies artifacts required for an audit (e.g., access review logs, SSO configuration screenshots, signed change approvals).
2. Evidence packaged into the evidence repository with metadata: control_id, owner, date_collected, collection_method.
3. Evidence retention per audit schedule (minimum 3 years for SOC2; longer per contract/regulatory requirement).

Storage & access:
- Official evidence store: encrypted internal repo (WORM-enabled blob store) with access limited to security, compliance, and auditors.
- Automated evidence collectors: scheduled exports for access reviews, system config baselines, and SSO logs.

Audit runbook (high level):
1. Kickoff: compliance requests scope and timeframe.
2. Control owner gathers artifacts and annotates them with context.
3. Compliance reviews artifacts; any gaps triaged as findings with remediation deadlines.
4. Final audit pack generated and securely delivered to auditors.

7) Risk Management & Exceptions

Risk assessment process:
- All security exceptions require a documented risk assessment: description, impacted assets, likelihood, impact, compensating controls, and expiry.
- Risk rating matrix (short):
  - Low: acceptable with monitoring
  - Medium: requires mitigation plan and 30-day remediation SLA
  - High: requires exec approval and compensating controls; temporary only (<= 7 days) unless explicitly extended

Exception request workflow:
1. Submit exception via the security exceptions portal with justification and proposed compensating controls.
2. Security reviews and assigns risk rating; medium/high escalated to Security Council for approval.
3. If approved, exception documented with owner and expiry date; automated reminders issued 7 days before expiry.

Compensating controls (examples):
- Use of restricted network segments + extra logging when full encryption or isolation cannot be achieved.
- Shorter TTLs for keys and additional manual approvals for privileged operations.

Reporting & metrics:
- Monthly exception dashboard: count by severity, average age, percent overdue.
- Quarterly risk review by Security Council including trending and open-high-risk items.
